related_questions.question: What does stage 2 grade 3 breast cancer mean?

text_blocks.snippet: In breast cancer, "stage 2 grade 3" means the cancer is localized (not spread to distant organs) but has some characteristics of a more aggressive cancer. Specifically, "stage 2" indicates the tumor is a moderate size or has spread to a few nearby lymph nodes, while "grade 3" signifies that the cancer cells, when viewed under a microscope, appear very different from normal breast cells and are likely to grow and spread more quickly.
snippet_highlighted_words: the cancer is localized (not spread to distant organs) but has some characteristics of a more aggressive cancer

list.title: Stage 2:
list.snippet: This stage suggests the tumor is either larger than 2 cm but still confined to the breast, or it has spread to a small number of nearby lymph nodes (typically up to three).

list.title: Grade 3:
list.snippet: This grade indicates that the cancer cells are "poorly differentiated," meaning they look very different from normal breast cells under a microscope and are likely to grow and spread more aggressively than lower-grade cancers.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, while the cancer hasn't spread far, the high grade suggests it might be more active and potentially more challenging to treat compared to lower-grade cancers at the same stage.
